reading: Backlit Plate has the field's clearest law for scarce light, and the judges value it for that. Light shows only through a cut in a matte plate, and the shape of the cut says what it shows: a slot is time, a round window is place, a 4:3 window is the screen. It came third in round 13 (7.8) with the most promise votes (5). Soul (8.4), system (8.4), interaction (8.5) and usability (8.7) praised its sight lines: one column, rule-led condensed heads with the figure and link at the right, stacked THU/1 day columns, WHO/DUE heads, the NOW divider, the amber-ticked late slot with its "2 late" link, the round radar window among the Ideas filters, and 0 small targets. What sank it is that on screen it read as plain. Style (6.4), feedback (7) and the skeptic (7) said the poetic idea did not show. The plate has no visible edge, bevel or seams, so it is one long admin sheet. Every row title is underlined; all eight lenses named this, so it is the single most-cited fix. Status is a bare single column with leaders running 600px. Settings, Family, Memory and Wishes are only restyled and keep rounded icon tiles. The 4:3 windows have spare glass. "mind" is stencilled but barely blooms, and the greeting lost its lit pool. The steel and denim companions are timid (82% green on Home). Add sits at the foot of To do. The open select drew as an empty band. The title "What's on your mind?" fails on every title panel. To win, the plate must be SEEN as a plate: a lit edge, an engraved bevel, seams between bands, and cuts whose light visibly spills onto a lip. The phosphor must come back at full strength in the cuts and only there. The underlines go. Status gets a real instrument and two columns. The grammar has to reach every page. The tour finals offer exactly the missing comprehension and figure devices: Waypoint's one day numeral, Departures' destination keys, Trued's lamp strip over a tally, and Waypoint's engraved placards. Each translates natively into "engraved in the plate" or "cut through the plate".

briefs.name: Plate, Engraved
briefs.hypothesis: Round 13 ranked the idea higher than the screen showed it. The law of light-only-through-a-cut won 5 promise votes and 8.4-8.7 from soul, system, interaction and usability, but style, feedback and the skeptic saw a plain dark admin page. This cross makes the plate physically legible: a lit plate edge and bevel, engraved seams between bands, and cuts whose light spills onto a lip. It puts the original tube's light back at full strength in those cuts: the E1 halo, E7's pool and scanlines, E12-E17 bevel spill and bloom. It removes the one fault every lens named (the underlined row titles). It also borrows three comprehension devices from the tour that are natively 'engraved' or 'cut': Waypoint's one day numeral, Departures' destination legends and Trued's lamp strip with its tally. Together these should lift the weak lenses (style, feedback, skeptic) toward 8 without losing the strong ones, and beat r13-idea-2's 7.8 and Desk Terminal, Joined's 7.54 on the landing scale.
briefs.brief:
Start from r13-idea-2's files (x14a-b/variants/r13-idea-2/: plate.css, sheet.css, tokens.json, templates/*). Keep: one centred slate plate over one lit screen; the cut vocabulary (slot = time, round = place, square = Vera, screen window = the screen proper, pinhole = lamp, stencil = the key word, backlit key = Send/primary, well = field); the rule-led condensed heads with the figure and link at the right; the one-column sight line on inner pages; and the six-step type scale (12/15/17/22/30/44), Instrument Sans narrow for heads, Plex Mono for figures, VT323 on glass only.

THE PLATE MADE VISIBLE (all pages). `.plate` (the page's main wrapper) gets a real edge. Add a 1px top lip `inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.06)`, a 1px dark groove `0 0 0 1px var(--groove)` and a second 1px `--lip` ring outside it. Add a faint green rim light that leaks round the plate's top edge only (E6/E8: `0 -1px 0 rgb(109 255 156 / 0.18)`, and a 40px `top-haze` above it from the bar). The plate face gets a barely-there anodised grain: `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.012) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px)` at 100% opacity on `--plate`, with no hue.

Bands are split by ENGRAVED SEAMS, `.seam`: a full-plate-width 2px `--groove` line with a 1px `--lip` highlight under it, running edge to edge through the plate's padding as a cut would. They go between Home's greeting, the setup band, and the Coming up / To do pair, and on every inner page between the head and the body. The existing lead rules (`.rule`) stay for section heads INSIDE a band. Seams split bands; rules head sections.

WINDOWS. `.win-screen`, `.win-round` and `.win-slot` all get one bevel treatment. Glass goes inside a 6px bevel (`--bevel`), and the bevel takes the screen's light as a gradient: lit on the bottom inner edge, dark on the top. Below each window the light SPILLS onto the plate as a 60-80px green pool, `radial-gradient(60% 100% at 50% 0%, rgb(109 255 156 / 0.10), transparent 70%)` on a `::after` under the bevel. This goes on Next up, the Ideas round window, the idea page's blip window (build it now: a round 7rem window with the idea's own blip, from the same radar macro), Status's spend window and every slot. Drop the forced 4:3 aspect: the screen window is sized to its words. Next up's window holds its VT323 lines and the 'N more' link with 1.2rem of glass around them.

HOME, desktop, top to bottom.
(1) The greeting band. Vera's square window (her screen, 40px) and the date are engraved above the question. The question is the 44px condensed head: 'Give Vera something to *plan*.' The word 'plan' is a STENCIL: E1 at full strength plus a hot core, `text-shadow: 0 0 0.12em rgb(220 255 230 / 0.6), 0 0 0.45em rgb(109 255 156 / 0.5), 0 0 1.3em rgb(109 255 156 / 0.25)`. Under it a light-leak: a 3px slot, the word's width, cut 6px below the baseline (`.stencil-leak`), lit `--brand` with blur(1px). It throws E7's pool with its scanlines (white 2.8%, 1px in 4, masked to the pool) down over the box's top lip, which gives back the lit pool from below. The textarea is a WELL whose cut edge lights on focus (E4). Send is the backlit key, with E3's pool out of its gap.
(2) The starters, beneath the box. They become one bank of three square engraved keys (no 4px radius: 2px), each with an engraved destination legend at its right end in 12px `--brass`: 'What should we do this weekend? · PLANS', 'Remind me to… · TO DO', 'We should try… · IDEAS'. A 3px left notch in the destination's grounded section ink (plans #70dcf4, todo #f7dc78, ideas #b58cec, each mixed 50% toward `--steel`) marks the key.
(3) To the right of the box (desktop), Next up: a content-sized screen window ('NEXT UP' plate, the plan name, 'Sun 4 Oct · 13:00 · in 2 days', '› 3 more on the slot'). A ROUND window is cut overlapping its lower-right corner, 8.5rem, carrying the radar with sweep, afterglow and blips (E17). This is the skeptic's 'round Next up radar on Home', and the shape grammar on show: a screen for what, a round for where. Under the pair sits an engraved placard (see Borrows).
(4) Seam. Finish setting up: one amber-led rule. Amber goes ONLY on the next step (step 1), with steps 2-3 in steel rings. Then three numbered rows, then seam.
(5) Two columns. Left, Coming up. The rule head reads 'Coming up' + '4 plans' (figure 600, word 400) + 'All plans →'. Then the fortnight SLOT window with labels at 14px Plex Mono (not VT323), NOW lit, and each plan's tick labelled with its DAY NUMERAL (4, 9, 17, 24). Then rows that lead with the same numeral (see Borrows): 'Next up, then 3 more' as the sub-figure so the count matches the rows. Right, To do. The head reads '4 open · 3 late · All 4 →' with the late slot's amber ticks. Rows are checkbox, title, who and due, with due as an amber words line under late titles. Then The kids' wishes and Something to eat as rule-headed lists.
(6) Lately added under Coming up: icon, title, kind word in its section ink (no underline), for, #.
(7) The STATUS FOOT. Delete the per-page READY chip everywhere and engrave one foot strip into the plate's bottom edge on every page (`.plate-foot`, above the site footer, inside the plate). It reads: pinhole lamp, 'Ready · OpenAI gpt-6-luna · $0.00 of $2.00 today', then 'Status →' at the right, all 15px, figures in Plex Mono. The lamp is lit, ringed red if stopped, or half amber if something needs a look.

HOME, phone (360-430px). Vera and the date, then the title on one or two lines at 34px, then the well, then From and Send (Send full width 48px), then the three destination keys stacked full width. Next comes Next up's screen window full width, with the round window cut at 6rem into its right edge. Then setup, Coming up's slot (the labels stay 14px; show 2 weeks), its rows, To do, and the foot. No horizontal scroll, 16px gutter.

ROWS, all pages. Row titles get NO underline at rest: `text-decoration: none`. Underline at 35% ink with a 3px offset appears on `:hover` and `:focus-visible`, full on hover. The whole row is the hit area (stretched link `::after`). Titles stay 600 `--ink`. Underlines remain for links in prose and in rule heads. Row afterglow: on hover a visible 12% `--steel` wash with a 2px sage (`--lit`) left edge. On leave it fades over 1.2s (`--row-fade`), so it is visible in a still.

TO DO. The page head is title + '4 open · 3 late' (figure 600, word 400) + 'Add something to do' as the green backlit primary at the head's right, which moves it up from the foot. Below it, the late slot, then the kind keys and search. The DUE column becomes the stacked day numeral (see Borrows), with 'was due 5 days ago' in amber words under the title on late rows. The NOW divider stays.

PLANS. The head is title + '4 coming' + List/Month keys + 'Add a plan' as primary. The slot labels use the day numerals at 14px. Month cells: the day numeral at 15px Plex Mono. Today is cut as a small lit square window around its numeral (not a steel chip). Event chips are square-cornered with a 3px plans-ink notch, times in mono.

IDEAS. One search, one bank of kind keys, the round window beside the filters with its bevel spill and placard ('PLACES · 15 MIN, 45 MIN, 2 H'). Rows: no underline.

STATUS (the plainest page today). The head reads 'Status' + the tally figure '5 working · 1 needs a look · 7 off' (figures 30px Plex Mono 500, words 15px) + 'Change the limit'. Under it, two windows side by side, joined by one bevel. Left, the spend SCREEN window, sized to words: '$0.00' in VT323 48px, the bar meter with a LIMIT tick at $2.00 and a ghost peak tick at the 30-day max. Right, a long SLOT window holding the 30-day spend trace (soul's fix: Status gets a trace). Below both runs the LAMP STRIP (see Borrows). Then seam, then the lists two across at ≥1100px (Who answers + Keys left, Connected to + Messages right). Each list is rule-headed with its 'n of m' figure, and each row is pinhole lamp, name, dotted leader, value. Rows are capped at 46rem: the value sits in a fixed right column of 16rem, wrapping, never 600px away.

SETTINGS, FAMILY, MEMORY, WISHES. Carry the grammar. The settings index loses its rounded icon tiles: it becomes engraved rows, each with the line icon at 20px in the icon column (`--icol`), the part's name 600, a dotted leader, the state in `--dim` and →, two across at desktop, split by rule heads ('The family', 'The machine', 'Sign-in'). 'Needs a look' becomes a half-amber pinhole plus amber words, not a pill. The group intro is aligned to the fields' left edge. Family: each person a row with a square engraved initial key (not a round avatar), role in `--brass`, who-may in words. Memory and Wishes: rule-led lists, wishes numbered in Plex Mono figures.

CONTROLS. Select (`.field select`): a well with a lit cut edge on focus. The open list is styled via `select, ::picker(select)` where supported, with `appearance: base-select`, `--surface-3` background, an `--edge` border and the selected option in `--brand` on `--on-bright`. The fallback is native with `color-scheme: dark`, so the capture is never an empty black band. Checkboxes are square 22px wells; checked fills `--brand` with an `--on-bright` tick; late ones get an amber cut edge. Focus is E5: a 2px `--brand` ring with 2px offset plus a 0.5em bloom.

COLOUR TOKENS (tokens.json). Keep bg #0b0e0c, surface #13181b, brand #6dff9c. Add `--brass: #a89a7c` (low-chroma warm, about 12% chroma) for ENGRAVED legends: placards, destination legends, role words, the foot's labels. This gives steel a warm partner and a second job, distinct from amber #ffb850, which stays 'late/next only'. Steel #6b8396 stays for structure: seams, lips, rings, the active nav. Target green share on Home ≤60%.
briefs.borrows:
The judges' fixes come from the dossier for r13-idea-2. (a) Row titles not underlined, underline on hover and focus only: all eight lenses (feedback, soul, style via 'plain', system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic). (b) Status given a lit instrument, a 30-day trace slot, a head figure, two columns, and leaders capped at 46rem with a 16rem value column: feedback, soul, type, usability, skeptic. (c) The plate made visible, with an edge, bevel, engraved seams between bands and cuts spilling onto a lip: style, skeptic, soul ('give the Ideas round window and the idea page's blip window the same spill'). (d) 'mind' given the full E1 halo plus a light-leak pool below: soul; lessons.md OPEN PROBLEMS, 'the greeting's lit pool from below was lost'. (e) Add up into the head as the green primary on To do and Plans: interaction, usability. (f) Plate grammar carried to Settings, Family, Memory and Wishes, no rounded tiles: system. (g) 4:3 windows sized to their words: system. (h) The per-page READY chip folded into one status foot linking to Status: system, interaction. (i) Slot labels at about 14px rather than VT323: interaction. (j) Amber off setup step 3 unless it means next: system. (k) The open select fixed: system, usability. (l) Head counts set as figure 600 + word 400, the stacked day column on To do's due, and the Settings intro aligned: type. (m) Coming up's count made to match its rows: usability. (n) A round Next up radar window on Home: skeptic, lessons FAILED REACHES. (o) A warmer second job for the steel companion: style.

From the other camp, rebuilt in the plate's terms.
1. ONE DAY NUMERAL, from Waypoint Lamps (t3-console-graft; files /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14a-b/variants/t3-console-graft/templates/home.html, the `.hop-day` spans at ~L185, and plans_month.html; sheet.css; shots x14a-b/out/t3-console-graft/shots/home.png). In the source, one light day figure (4, 9, 17, 24) sits in the route ring and leads the row; interaction 8 called it 'the best comprehension device in the heat'. Here the numeral is ENGRAVED on the plate at 30px (the scale's 'figures' step) in Plex Mono 400 tabular `--heading`, with 'Oct / Sun' stacked at 12px `--dim` beside it. It leads every Coming up row, every To do due cell and every Plans list row. The same numeral, in VT323 on the glass, labels that plan's tick in the slot window and the month cell. Use ONE face for the mark off-glass (Plex Mono); the type judge faulted Waypoint for mixing mono 500 and sans 300.
2. DESTINATION LEGENDS ON THE STARTERS, from Departures, Platformed (t3-timetable-refine; files /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14a-a/variants/t3-timetable-refine/templates/_ask.html L60-68 (`.key-to`, `to-plans` etc.) and sheet.css L107, L1524-1541; shots x14a-a/out/t3-timetable-refine/shots/home.png). Interaction 8 called 'usually Plans / To do / Ideas' 'the best comprehension aid in the heat'. Here each starter is a square engraved key with its destination engraved at its right end in 12px uppercase `--brass` (+0.06em tracking, the only tracked caps), plus a 3px notch of that section's ink mixed toward steel. That is a grounded solid with a job, not enamel. The words 'usually' go in the sr-only text.
3. LAMP STRIP OVER A TALLY on Status, from Trued, Relit (t3-track-refine2; files /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14a-a/variants/t3-track-refine2/templates/status.html L55-135 (the banks, `.bank-lamps`, the `lamps` namespace count and the `.tally` line); shots x14a-a/out/t3-track-refine2/shots/status.png). System 8 praised 'Status opens on a glass strip of lamps over a tally'. Here it becomes one long row of PINHOLES drilled through the plate, grouped in three banks ('Who answers 3 of 4', 'Keys 1 of 4', 'Connected 2 of 5') split by engraved ticks. Each pinhole is lit green (E20 breathe), ringed red when stopped, half amber when it needs a look, or a dark empty hole when not set up, with its 12px `--brass` name engraved beneath. The tally line under it reads as the legend: each figure 30px Plex Mono followed by the lamp shape it counts and its word. The tally also becomes Status's head figure.
4. (ledger) ENGRAVED PLACARD / CHIN LEGEND under each window, from Waypoint Lamps' placards (T3-29; x14a-b/variants/t3-console-graft/sheet.css L1705-1723 `.placard`, `_ui.html` crt macro) and the ledger's L193 'An instrument chin that names its scale' (r11-idea-2 Long Persistence; rounds/r11/variants/r11-idea-2/palette.css L429-452 `.chin`, `.chin-legend`; _ui.html L135-140). Here every window gets ONE short engraved line on the plate just under its bevel spill, 12px `--brass` with an engraved text-shadow (`0 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6), 0 -1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.05)`), aria-hidden where it repeats visible text. It must name a true scale and never explain: 'PLANS · 1 WK/DIV' under Coming up's slot, 'DUE · 1 WK/DIV' under To do's, 'PLACES · 15 MIN · 45 MIN · 2 H' under the round windows, 'SPEND · LIMIT $2.00' under the spend window, '30 DAYS · $1.26' under the trace, and 'NO SIGNAL' on the 404. The skeptic's split vote ('over-explains') is answered by keeping it to the scale, one line.
briefs.avoids: It answers every-row-title-underlined (all lenses) with no underline at rest and the whole row as the hit area. It answers 'calm to the point of plain', 'one long slate sheet', 'the plate idea needs to show' (style, feedback, skeptic) with a visible plate edge and rim light, engraved seams between bands, bevel spill on every window and full-strength phosphor in the cuts. It answers 'mind barely blooms' and the lost greeting pool (soul, lessons) with the hot-core stencil and its leak slot throwing E7's pool and scanlines. It answers bare Status (feedback, skeptic, usability, type) with a screen window plus a trace slot, a lamp strip over a tally, two columns and capped leaders. 'Settings and Family only restyled, rounded tiles' (system) gets engraved rows with no tiles. Spare 4:3 glass (system) goes: windows are sized to words. 'Add at the foot' (interaction, usability) becomes a head primary. 'Timid steel and denim, 82% green' (style, feedback) gets a warm brass for engraved legends, section-ink notches on the destination keys and a green share target ≤60%. 'Empty black band' for the select becomes a styled picker with a dark-scheme fallback. Also answered: amber on a non-next setup step (system), '5 plans over 4 rows' (usability), small VT323 slot labels (interaction), and the generic 'What's on your mind?' title that every title panel failed. It also avoids the tour's known traps: no green rail across the page (glare), no bay-inside-a-bay boxes (Waypoint's fault), no round pilot-lamp checkboxes reading as radios, no amber minus badges, and no tracked caps on nav or buttons (only the 12px engraved legends).
briefs.title: 'Give Vera something to *plan*.' This title has NOT been tried in the tour or the crossing rounds. It keeps what the panels rewarded in 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (8.02, 8.01): it names who hears you, and it is an imperative the box beneath answers, so it reads as an instruction to type, not 'show me the plan'. The job word 'plan', lit, lands at the full stop where the eye stops. 'Something' is broader than 'what to plan': a reminder, an idea to keep or a wish is all 'something to plan', which answers the judges' worry that 'plan' alone leaves out ideas and reminders. It can't be answered yes/no ('Anything to plan?' failed for that), and 'give' fits the plate's metaphor: you hand her something through the cut. It sets on one line at 44px condensed on desktop and on two lines on a phone, breaking after 'Vera'. The lineage's own 'What's on your mind?' is dropped: every title panel failed it as generic.
